Introduction and Clarification:
We are creating three linear models with different independent variable combinations:
Model 1: Technology + Class
Model 2: Technology + Net Capacity Factor
Model 3: Technology + Annual Energy Generation

All work are done collectively as a team.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(readxl)
library(openxlsx)

#Load in data
Solar_ATB <- read.csv("Processed_Data/Solar_ATB_Long.csv")
```

```{r}
Solar_ATB <- Solar_ATB %>%
  select(-"X")

Model1.lm <- lm(LCOE ~
                Technology +
                Class,
                data = Solar_ATB)
summary(Model1.lm)
plot(Model1.lm)

AIC(Model1.lm)

view(Solar_ATB)

```


```{r}
# Remove data point 
Solar_ATB_Model1.2 <- Solar_ATB[-c(125,137,142),]
Model1.2.lm <- lm(LCOE ~
                Technology +
                Class,
             data = Solar_ATB_Model1.2)
summary(Model1.2.lm)
plot(Model1.2.lm)
AIC(Model1.2.lm)
```


```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
Model2.lm <- lm(LCOE ~
                Technology +
                Net_Capacity_Factor,
             data = Solar_ATB)
summary(Model2.lm)
plot(Model2.lm)
AIC(Model2.lm)
```

```{r}
# Remove data point 1,29,30
Solar_ATB_Model2.2 <- Solar_ATB[-c(137,142,147),]
Model2.2.lm <- lm(LCOE ~
                Technology +
                Net_Capacity_Factor,
             data = Solar_ATB_Model2.2)
summary(Model2.2.lm)
plot(Model2.2.lm)
AIC(Model2.2.lm)
```

```{r}
# Model variable: Technology and generation
Model3.lm <- lm(LCOE ~
                Technology +
                log(Annual_Generation_MWh),
             data = Solar_ATB)
summary(Model3.lm)
plot(Model3.lm)
```
```{r}
# Remove data point 1,29,30
Solar_ATB_Model3.2 <- Solar_ATB[-c(95,110,125),]
Model3.2.lm <- lm(LCOE ~
                Technology +
                log(Annual_Generation_MWh),
             data = Solar_ATB_Model3.2)
summary(Model3.2.lm)
plot(Model3.2.lm)
AIC(Model3.2.lm)
```
As we can conclude Model 3 may be the best prediction for LCOE with highest adjusted R-squared value and lowest AIC value, although all three models have great predictions with significant p value (P<0.0001).
